Install Snurpo

Download Snurpo 1.5.0 from the published GitHub release. The desktop packages include the capture engine and companion MCP executable. Node.js, Rust and a model account are not required to run them.

Choose your download#

ComputerPackage
macOS, Apple SiliconSnurpo-v1.5.0-macOS-arm64.zip
Windows, x64Snurpo-v1.5.0-Windows-x64-setup.exe
Linux, x64AppImage or Debian package

There is no Intel macOS or Linux arm64 package in this release. Windows and Linux packages have CI build and headless protocol coverage; interactive installers, desktop use and device behavior on those hosts remain unverified. Native interaction has been exercised on macOS Apple Silicon.

Verify and open#

Compare your file's SHA-256 with SHA256SUMS.txt. For example, on macOS:

sh
shasum -a 256 Snurpo-v1.5.0-macOS-arm64.zip

On Windows, use Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 in PowerShell; on Linux, use sha256sum.

On macOS, extract the ZIP, move Snurpo.app into Applications and open it. The app is ad-hoc signed, not Apple-notarized. After verifying the download, use System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway if macOS blocks the first launch. Keep Gatekeeper enabled.

On Windows, run the x64 installer. On Linux, use the package appropriate for your distribution. An AppImage needs executable permission:

sh
chmod +x Snurpo-v1.5.0-Linux-x64.AppImage
./Snurpo-v1.5.0-Linux-x64.AppImage

Linux has a tracked glib dependency advisory; see the dependency record for its status and boundaries.

Updating an existing installation#

Quit the old app before opening the new one. Scope and Snurpo share the same archive and CA; do not run both at once or rename their data files. Back up important captures before an upgrade. Compatibility details.

Optional Frida binaries are not bundled. You only need them for the Frida Android workflow, not ordinary desktop capture.
